project.name: radar-guard-gsd
project.description: Radar-Guard is a field-worker safety management agent that combines non-contact radar sensing with a vector database for high-security site monitoring; this repository holds the RAG/UI portion of the project (LangChain, pgvector, a Streamlit dashboard) built for the 2026 Hanium Dream-Up contest.

nodes.name: console_ui.py
nodes.summary: Main PyQt5 desktop application for the Radar-Guard safety console — builds all screens, side navigation, and the app entry point, while importing detection/logic classes from radar_core.py so the UI layer never re-implements judgment logic.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately separates screen/UI code from detection logic (imported wholesale from radar_core.py, not copy-pasted) so that changing a screen and changing a judgment path are always distinguishable in the diff — important for a safety system's accountability.

nodes.name: facility.py
nodes.summary: Defines the facility floor plan (walls, equipment outlines, monitored zones, radar positions, exits, evacuation routes) as pure data with zero dependencies, so a new site can be onboarded by editing coordinates only.

nodes.name: radar_core.py
nodes.summary: Logic and shared-widget layer for the Radar-Guard console: UDP radar link reception, pose estimation, pgvector/LLM-based SOP search, 3D point-cloud visualization widgets, and settings/evidence/power popups — all screen-independent so console_ui.py can render the UI without duplicating detection logic.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses background threads and lru_cache for non-blocking SOP retrieval-augmented-generation search via langchain_ollama/PGVector, with a RAG_OK feature flag that gracefully disables SOP search if the local Ollama/pgvector stack isn't running.

nodes.name: resolve_font
nodes.summary: Resolves the best available UI font by checking installed font families against a candidate list (Pretendard, Noto Sans KR, etc.), falling back to Malgun Gothic so layout never silently breaks on machines without the preferred font.

nodes.name: lb

nodes.name: button

nodes.name: styled_combo

nodes.name: scrollable
nodes.summary: Wraps an inner widget in a themed QScrollArea, optionally with a horizontal scrollbar.

nodes.name: as_page

nodes.name: apply_dark_palette
nodes.summary: Applies the app's dark color palette (background, panel, text, highlight colors) to the QApplication so all widgets inherit consistent dark theming.

nodes.name: build_app
nodes.summary: Application bootstrap function that constructs the QApplication, applies the dark palette/font, instantiates the RadarLink connection (live or demo), and creates the main ConsoleV2 window; reused by both main() and the regression test scripts to drive the UI headlessly.

nodes.name: main

nodes.name: StatusDot

nodes.name: StatusCard

nodes.name: MetricTile

nodes.name: SideView

nodes.name: SceneView
nodes.summary: Container widget managing 3D/2D scene rendering mode switching (falls back to 2D when OpenGL is unavailable) and camera reset.

nodes.name: ZoneStrip
nodes.summary: Custom-painted widget rendering a horizontal strip of monitored-zone status indicators.

nodes.name: FacilityPlan
nodes.summary: Interactive floor-plan widget drawing walls, equipment, radar coverage zones, evacuation routes, and a live worker position, with hover/click zone selection.

nodes.name: Timeline
nodes.summary: Widget rendering a scrolling event-timeline strip that flips and adds entries over time.

nodes.name: SopView

nodes.name: EvidenceView
nodes.summary: Widget rendering evidence details (pose/detection snapshot) for a specific safety event.

nodes.name: ActionDrawer
nodes.summary: Slide-in in-app drawer widget (cannot leave the window, unlike v1's detachable popup) presenting the recommended action for an active alarm, with open/close animation.

nodes.name: DashboardPage
nodes.summary: Main overview screen showing zone status, live metrics, recent events, and alarm counts; the landing page of the console.

nodes.name: MonitorPage
nodes.summary: Live monitoring screen combining the 3D/2D scene view, facility plan, pose readout, and zone legend for real-time worker tracking.

nodes.name: EventLogPage
nodes.summary: Screen listing historical safety events with resolve and export actions.

nodes.name: SopGuidePage
nodes.summary: Screen for browsing and selecting SOP documents by category.

nodes.name: AiIconButton
nodes.summary: Custom-painted floating action button that opens the AI assistant drawer.

nodes.name: AssistantDrawer

nodes.name: SideNav
nodes.summary: Left sidebar navigation widget with page selection, user display, and alarm-driven locking (navigation is locked while an alarm is unacknowledged so workers can't wander away from an active alarm screen).

nodes.name: SopEngineV2
nodes.summary: Background-threaded SOP retrieval engine for the assistant drawer: builds a fact block from live sensor state and searches/generates guidance without blocking the UI thread.

nodes.name: ConsoleV2

nodes.name: to_plan
nodes.summary: Converts radar-local coordinates (cx, cz) for a zone into facility floor-plan coordinates by adding the radar's installed position offset; returns None for zones without an installed radar.

nodes.name: coverage
nodes.summary: Returns the detection-coverage rectangle (x, y, w, h) for a zone's installed radar, centered on its position with a fixed half-width (COVER_HALF).

nodes.name: lb
nodes.summary: Styled QLabel factory helper — radar_core's own copy of the label-building pattern used by the popups defined in this module.

nodes.name: btn

nodes.name: panel

nodes.name: titled

nodes.name: confirm
nodes.summary: Shows a themed modal confirmation dialog (yes/no, with optional danger styling) and returns the user's choice.

nodes.name: md_to_html
nodes.summary: Converts a small subset of Markdown (used in SOP guidance text) into HTML for display in Qt rich-text labels.

nodes.name: stick_segments
nodes.summary: Computes 3D line segments for a stick-figure body-pose visualization from a center point, axis, and length.

nodes.name: _facility_reference_lines
nodes.summary: Builds reference line geometry (floor grid / facility outline) for the 3D scene widget.

nodes.name: _mannequin_mesh
nodes.summary: Builds a 3D mesh approximating a human figure for pose visualization.

nodes.name: body_mesh
nodes.summary: Generates the 3D body-mesh geometry for a tracked worker at a given position and orientation.

nodes.name: search_sop_documents
nodes.summary: Queries the pgvector-backed SOP document store for entries relevant to an event type/situation/category, used by SopEngine before optional LLM summarization.

nodes.name: Dialog
nodes.summary: Minimal themed base QDialog used by the module's popups.

nodes.name: RadarLink
nodes.summary: Background thread managing the UDP connection to the Jetson radar unit — sends hello/control commands and periodically emits link-age/status so the UI can show connection health; the system remains fail-safe if this link drops because the Jetson keeps judging and cutting power independently.

nodes.name: PoseEstimator
nodes.summary: Accumulates N frames of point-cloud data and estimates worker pose via PCA for on-screen 3D visualization only — explicitly documented as not feeding back into the safety detection/judgment path.

nodes.name: SopEngine
nodes.summary: Background-threaded SOP retrieval engine: on request, performs vector search via search_sop_documents and an optional LLM (Gemma) summarization pass, with a prewarm step to reduce first-query latency.

nodes.name: Track3D
nodes.summary: 3D point-cloud widget for the live monitor screen — renders detected points, computes figure/body geometry via stick_segments/body_mesh, and automatically falls back to a 2D projection when OpenGL is unavailable.

nodes.name: PreparePage
nodes.summary: Screen guiding the empty-room scan, baseline collection, and autoencoder training workflow that must complete before a zone can go live.

nodes.name: SettingsPopup
nodes.summary: Settings dialog with tabs for AI/SOP configuration (document ingestion, prescan, model test) plus other diagnostic settings — the single place model names, ports, and thresholds are exposed, deliberately moved out of the operator-facing dashboard.

nodes.name: EvidencePopup
nodes.summary: Popup dialog showing evidence details for a specific event, mirroring EvidenceView for standalone use.

nodes.name: PowerPopup
nodes.summary: Popup showing per-zone power/breaker state and trip status, with a refresh action.

nodes.name: RestorePopup
nodes.summary: Confirmation popup for restoring power to a tripped zone after an alarm has been resolved.

nodes.name: QueryPopup
nodes.summary: Standalone popup version of the AI assistant query/answer interface.

nodes.name: GraphPopup
nodes.summary: Popup displaying a pyqtgraph plot (e.g., a sensor time series) pushed from the live feed.

nodes.name: _DemoSource

nodes.name: 테스트_v1결함_재발검사.py
nodes.summary: Headless PyQt regression test (offscreen Qt platform) that drives the v2 console UI end to end to verify that UI defects previously fixed in v1 have not resurfaced — checks nav/drawer interplay, dialog theming, and AI assistant response routing.

nodes.name: 테스트_레이아웃_검증.py
nodes.summary: Headless UI layout verification script that renders the console at multiple window sizes and scans the widget tree for text-clipping and sibling-widget overlap regressions.

nodes.name: check_clipping
nodes.summary: Walks the visible widget tree and flags any QLabel/QPushButton whose rendered width is narrower than its measured text width, catching text-clipping layout regressions (skips widgets inside collapsed/animating drawers).

nodes.name: check_overlap
nodes.summary: Walks sibling widgets under a parent and flags rectangle intersections that indicate unintended layout overlap, excluding intentional overlays like veils and drawers.

nodes.name: radar_common.py
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for the constants, coordinate/physics parameters, network settings, and Korean display-label lookups that must stay identical between the Jetson sensor script and the laptop console UI, created after those values were found duplicated and silently drifting apart.
nodes.languageNotes: Stdlib-only module (no numpy/torch/Qt) so it can be imported unmodified on both the Jetson and the laptop; most of its size is flat constant tables rather than logic.

nodes.name: replay_jsonl.py
nodes.summary: Replays previously recorded real radar point-cloud JSONL captures over the same UDP protocol jetson_sender uses, driving the laptop console UI with genuine sensor data (without re-running fall classification) to verify the display pipeline renders real inputs correctly.
nodes.languageNotes: Explicitly re-applies the same near-field point filter jetson_sender uses on raw captures, reasoning that skipping it would make the laptop's pose estimator misread sensor self-reflections as a person standing at ceiling height.

nodes.name: sim_jetson.py
nodes.summary: Mock Jetson UDP sender that fabricates synthetic point-cloud scenarios (warmup, training, walking, falling) using only numpy/stdlib, letting the laptop console UI's protocol and display path be exercised end-to-end without a real radar or torch dependency.
nodes.languageNotes: Zone strings were previously hardcoded to a non-existent zone; the file now sources SIM_ZONE from radar_common.RADAR_ZONE as a single source of truth so the simulated equipment location matches the one real installed radar.

nodes.name: 테스트_실데이터_재생.py
nodes.summary: Offscreen automated integration test that drives replay_jsonl.py's real-data replay over UDP into console_ui.py and radar_core.py, then asserts UI state (alarm color, evidence panel, SOP guidance, rendered skeleton segments) matches expectations across still and fall event scenarios.
nodes.languageNotes: Forces QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen plus an explicit QT_QPA_FONTDIR on Windows after measuring that the offscreen Qt plugin silently loads zero fonts otherwise, which was producing false text-clipping failures unrelated to the actual UI code.

nodes.name: 테스트_평면도_경보흐름.py
nodes.summary: Short offscreen smoke test that replays still and fall events through replay_jsonl.py into console_ui.py and asserts the facility floor-plan's pre-alert, alarm-latch/auto-navigation, and zone-click flows all behave correctly.
nodes.languageNotes: Written as a flat top-level script (module-level asserts, not wrapped in main()) aside from two small helper functions, so most of its UI-driving calls happen outside any function body.

nodes.name: zone_equipped
nodes.summary: Returns whether a given zone id has physical breaker/equipment installed, via the ZONE_EQUIPPED lookup table.

nodes.name: pg_conn_str

nodes.name: parse_pre_alert

nodes.name: event_sev

nodes.name: sev_color
nodes.summary: Maps a severity level to its display color (green/amber/red) via the SEV_COLOR table; used both by console_ui and by integration tests to assert the correct alert color was rendered.

nodes.name: gate_ko
nodes.summary: Returns the Korean display label for a given detection-gate key from GATE_META.

nodes.name: gate_why

nodes.name: event_ko
nodes.summary: Returns the Korean display label for an event type from the EVENT_KO table.

nodes.name: zone_ko
nodes.summary: Returns the Korean display label for a zone id from the ZONE_KO table.

nodes.name: prefilter
nodes.summary: Drops radar points closer than NEAR_FIELD_MIN_RANGE, mirroring jetson_sender's own near-field filtering so replayed data matches production preprocessing exactly.

nodes.name: log
nodes.summary: Appends a timestamped message to the shared log buffer and prints it to the console.

nodes.name: load_events
nodes.summary: Loads a recorded events JSONL file, prefiltering each frame's point cloud and normalizing per-event fields (label, evidence, gates) into a list of event dicts for replay.

nodes.name: summarize
nodes.summary: Loads an events file and returns per-label event counts, used for the --list CLI report.

nodes.name: cmd_list
nodes.summary: Implements the --list CLI command, printing per-file event/label counts across all discoverable JSONL capture files.

nodes.name: control_listener
nodes.summary: Runs a UDP socket loop listening for control commands (HELLO, train, reset, resolve, restore) sent by the console UI and updates shared network/breaker state in response.

nodes.name: _pack

nodes.name: _evidence_from
nodes.summary: Builds an evidence summary dict (height/displacement/speed min-max-range statistics) from a window of recorded frames, for display in the alert evidence panel.

nodes.name: _gates_from
nodes.summary: Converts a recorded gates dict into a normalized active-gates summary used when firing a simulated event.

nodes.name: _fire

nodes.name: _clear
nodes.summary: Clears an active alert back to the normal state, logging the current breaker states and resetting per-event fields.

nodes.name: play_event
nodes.summary: Plays back a single event's recorded point-cloud frames at a chosen speed, waiting through pre-alert and hold windows and calling _fire/_clear to simulate the full alert lifecycle in real time.

nodes.name: scenario
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a full replay session, grouping loaded events by label, selecting them per the requested sequence (or randomly), and playing them one after another via play_event.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Defines the AI_BRIDGE communication protocol for the radar-guard-gsd project: the single-source-of-truth role of each document (REVIEW.md, INBOX.md, OUTBOX.md, HANDOFF.md, BACKLOG.md, git log, ADRs), the triage workflow connecting GPT, Cowork (Claude), Claude Code and the user, and the operating rules governing how items move between these documents.
nodes.languageNotes: Written in Korean; an internal multi-agent process specification, not user-facing product documentation. Defines strict rules (max 10 open items, no direct GPT-to-INBOX writes, full-rewrite-only HANDOFF updates) enforced by companion validation scripts.

nodes.summary: Queue of already-triaged requests, proposals and decisions from the user, GPT and Cowork awaiting action by Claude Code, currently covering a Qt UI skill install, pending approval to trim CLAUDE.md, and handoff instructions for a two-day Codex-only work period during a credit outage.

nodes.name: REVIEW.md

nodes.languageNotes: Never read by Claude Code by design — it is the deliberative scratchpad for GPT and Cowork; only agreed conclusions are moved out to INBOX.md, an ADR, or BACKLOG.md and deleted from this file.

tour.title: Project Overview & Dev Log
tour.description: Start with README.md, a reverse-chronological Korean engineering dev-log (~3,665 lines) documenting every work session on Radar-Guard, a contactless-radar-sensing safety agent built for the 2026 Hanium Dream-Up contest. It records the project's real history as dated problem-to-solution entries -- RF tuning, fall-classifier training, Jetson integration, RAG/SOP work -- giving you the authentic narrative before you look at any code. Notice its own warning that the canonical working copy moved to a different path on 2026-08-10: a first hint that this repository holds parallel and superseded material rather than one clean codebase.

tour.title: Folder Map: Real vs. Legacy vs. Experimental
tour.description: Before touching any code, read this folder guide -- arguably the single most important orientation document in the repo. It explains the numbered top-level layout (01_현행코드 through 10_팀협업, plus archive folders), states which files matter day-to-day, and warns which paths must never be moved because verification scripts and classifier training depend on their exact location. Keep its lesson for the rest of this tour: 01_현행코드 is the live production system, 02_레이더_원본코드 is the historical original it was split from, 10_팀협업 holds a teammate's parallel variant, and 06_부스_하우징 is an unrelated hardware-CAD track.

tour.title: Working Rules & the Architecture Split
tour.description: CLAUDE.md is the canonical rulebook read every session by Claude Code and Cowork, and it defines the core architectural principle behind everything you're about to see: the Jetson edge device judges danger and can cut power independently, while the laptop console only displays and never gates the safety decision. AGENTS.md is a generated mirror of CLAUDE.md, kept identical for Codex-based agents -- it must never be hand-edited directly, only regenerated by a sync script you'll meet in the final step of this tour. Together they set the folder ownership, forbidden actions, and mandatory verification commands that every production file from here on was built under.

tour.title: Production Entry Point: console_ui.py
tour.description: This is the main PyQt5 desktop application and the closest thing this repo has to a conventional entry point. It builds every screen and the side navigation, but deliberately imports all detection/judgment logic from radar_core.py instead of re-implementing it, so a diff touching a screen is always distinguishable from a diff touching a safety-judgment path. That separation is a direct, concrete consequence of the Jetson/laptop split you just read about in CLAUDE.md.
tour.languageLesson: The app is bootstrapped through a single build_app() factory that constructs the QApplication, palette, and main window; both main() and the headless (offscreen-Qt) regression tests call the same factory, so production startup and automated tests exercise identical code.

tour.title: Detection Logic & RAG-Based SOP Search
tour.description: radar_core.py is the screen-independent logic and shared-widget layer that console_ui.py depends on: it manages the UDP link to the Jetson (RadarLink), pose visualization, and -- central to this repo's RAG/UI mission -- a pgvector/LangChain-based Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) search that looks up safety guidance for a detected event. A RAG_OK feature flag lets the console keep running if the local Ollama/pgvector stack isn't up, and the search itself runs on a background thread so it never blocks the UI. This is the file where the project's two halves -- radar sensing and vector-DB retrieval -- actually meet.
tour.languageLesson: Background threads plus lru_cache give non-blocking retrieval-augmented search; a graceful-degradation feature flag (RAG_OK) is a useful pattern whenever a UI depends on an optional local service.

tour.title: Shared Constants: The Single Source of Truth
tour.description: radar_common.py has the highest fan-in of any file in the codebase: it holds every constant, coordinate/physics parameter, network setting, and Korean display-label lookup that must stay identical between the Jetson sensor script and the laptop console you just toured. It was created after these values were found silently drifting apart on each side of the Jetson/laptop split -- direct evidence for why CLAUDE.md insists edge and display logic stay separate but synchronized.

tour.title: Site Data Model: facility.py
tour.description: facility.py defines the monitored facility as pure data -- walls, equipment outlines, zones, radar positions, exits, and evacuation routes -- with zero code dependencies, so a new site can be onboarded by editing coordinates alone. console_ui.py's floor-plan widget renders directly from this file, which means the whole console can be repointed at a different physical site without touching any UI or detection code.

tour.title: Edge Pipeline: jetson_sender.py
tour.description: This is the large Jetson-side counterpart to everything you've seen so far: it implements the actual end-to-end pipeline running on the edge device -- LMS signal filtering, feature extraction, rule-based and ML (random-forest, LSTM autoencoder) fall/anomaly classification, and Modbus relay/circuit-breaker control. It streams results to the laptop console over the socket protocol whose shared constants live in radar_common.py (Step 6), and because it makes the power-cutting decision independently of the laptop, it's what makes the fail-safe architecture from CLAUDE.md real rather than aspirational.
tour.languageLesson: Combining a classical model (random forest) with a learned anomaly detector (LSTM autoencoder) is a common hybrid pattern in safety-critical pipelines: interpretable rules catch known failure modes while the learned model catches novel ones.

tour.title: Sensor Config & Training Data
tour.description: radar_guard.cfg is the production TI IWR6843ISK-ODS sensor configuration sent to the radar's serial port at startup -- tuned for fall detection with a 0-5m range and ±3 m/s doppler window, with clutter removal deliberately disabled so a stationary post-fall pose keeps registering. events_fall_5people_20260813_1.jsonl is real labeled training data captured on 2026-08-13 across 5 people, each line a session of 20-frame point-cloud windows with a fall label -- this is the actual data jetson_sender.py's classifiers (Step 8) were trained and validated against.
tour.languageLesson: JSONL (newline-delimited JSON) lets a dataset be streamed and appended to one labeled session at a time without rewriting the whole file -- convenient for incrementally growing training data from field tests.

tour.title: The RAG/UI Learning Journal
tour.description: Before the pgvector/LangChain SOP search inside radar_core.py (Step 5) could be built, the RAG/UI contributor worked through a personal study track kept under 08_주차별_진행도. The Week 1 document explains RAG, LangChain, and pgvector fundamentals from scratch, and the Week 4 document sketches a combined Streamlit dashboard for sensor monitoring plus RAG guidance -- the conceptual seed of the SOP-search feature that eventually shipped inside radar_core.py rather than as a separate Streamlit app. This journal is deliberately kept apart from production code: it is a learning trail, not something any production file imports.

tour.title: Testing Without Hardware
tour.description: These two scripts let the production UI be exercised without a real radar attached. sim_jetson.py fabricates synthetic point-cloud scenarios (warmup, walking, falling) using only numpy, while replay_jsonl.py replays a real captured session like the one from Step 9 over the same UDP protocol jetson_sender.py uses -- driving console_ui.py with genuine sensor data to verify the display pipeline without re-running classification. Together they let the team iterate on the UI/detection-display path quickly while actual hardware is offline or unavailable.
tour.languageLesson: Recording real production traffic and replaying it deterministically (replay_jsonl.py) is often more trustworthy for regression testing than hand-written synthetic fixtures alone (sim_jetson.py) -- which is why this project keeps both approaches side by side.

tour.title: Legacy Lineage: The Original Reference Implementation
tour.description: Stepping outside 01_현행코드: radar_live_full.py under 02_레이더_원본코드 is the flagship original -- a single monolithic script implementing the full radar-to-SOP pipeline (LMS filtering, LSTM autoencoder, classification, RAG-based SOP generation) with a 5-phase workflow and a matplotlib live dashboard. radar_parser.py is its serial-interface counterpart, sending a config like radar_guard.cfg to the sensor and parsing raw TLV frames. Per 폴더안내.md's guidance from Step 2, this whole folder is historical: it was later split apart into the leaner, better-separated 01_현행코드 modules you toured in Steps 4-8, so read it to understand where the current architecture came from, not as something to modify.

tour.title: Team Variant: A Parallel Implementation
tour.description: radar_live_full_option.py under 10_팀협업 is a teammate's alternate full pipeline: it adds its own LMS adaptive filtering and static-clutter removal, real-data model training, and a richer step-by-step UI progress renderer for live demos. It was developed independently alongside both the legacy reference (Step 12) and the current production code (Steps 4-8), illustrating a recurring pattern in this repo: multiple contributors converging on a similar sense-classify-RAG-SOP architecture without a shared library, because the numbered-folder structure keeps everyone's work isolated rather than merged.

tour.title: A Different Domain: Booth Hardware CAD
tour.description: gen_housing.py under 06_부스_하우징 is a complete change of subject from everything else in this tour: a parametric 3D CAD generator, built with trimesh boolean operations, that produces the physical enclosure tray, cable strain relief, mounting bosses, and lid for the radar hardware booth, based on measured board dimensions. It has no software dependency on any file you've seen so far -- it exists because the contest also requires a physical booth, and this folder is the CAD track for that hardware, entirely separate from the detection/RAG software domain.

tour.title: How the Repo Governs Itself
tour.description: Closing the loop on the working rules from Step 3: HANDOFF.md is the strictly bounded (40-line max) cross-session handoff note that is the sole execution-instruction channel between Codex/Claude Code and Cowork sessions. The .githooks/pre-commit hook enforces discipline at commit time -- it blocks commits touching HANDOFF.md/AI_BRIDGE without passing validation, and rejects any commit to 01_현행코드/*.py that isn't accompanied by a HANDOFF.md update. sync_agent_docs.py is what keeps AGENTS.md mechanically identical to CLAUDE.md (Step 3) instead of letting them hand-drift, and can itself run as that same pre-commit gate -- together these three files show how this multi-lineage, multi-agent repository enforces consistency without a CI server.
tour.languageLesson: A shell pre-commit hook plus small Python validation scripts is a lightweight alternative to full CI for enforcing repo conventions locally -- at the cost of relying on every contributor having hooks installed (.githooks requires `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` to activate).
